versions.summary: The prompt as E2 ran it.
How a finding cites: one turn, the shortest exact span, nothing in the statement beyond the quote.
added: Cite each finding with the one turn that states it. Quote only the shortest span of that turn that carries the fact, with every number, name and date the statement uses, and make the statement say no more than the quote does.

versions.summary: The v1 abstain line is replaced by when to abstain and when not to, so both sides of abstention are addressed.
added: Abstain only when no turn states the answer: set status to abstained, leave findings empty, and say in missing what is not stated. A turn that mentions the topic without the answer, or a guess from what people usually do, is not an answer.
When a turn does state the answer, give it, even if it is short or the speaker is not sure; do not abstain.
removed: If the turns do not answer the question, say so and abstain.

versions.summary: At most 3 findings, one short sentence each, short quotes and notes.
added: Keep the card short: at most 3 findings, each statement one sentence of at most 25 words, each quote at most 30 words, and each note in missing one sentence.

config.selection_rule: Each candidate version is compared with the baseline v1 on the same cases. score(v) is the mean of grounded_rate and the lower of abstain_when_insufficient and answer_when_answerable (the weaker abstention side); a version whose three metrics are not all defined is not eligible. A candidate qualifies only if (1) it has a measurable gain: the 95% interval of its difference from v1 on grounded_rate or on abstain_when_insufficient lies above zero, (2) it has no measurable loss: the interval of its difference from v1 on none of grounded_rate, abstain_when_insufficient and answer_when_answerable lies below zero, and (3) its score is above v1's. The chosen version is the qualifier with the highest score, ties broken by lower median latency, then by the order of VERSIONS. With no qualifier the baseline v1 is kept and the record says there was no measurable improvement. A version whose output was invalid or timed out too often to be measured is listed in attempts and cannot qualify. Respond mode and injected claims are reported for every version and do not enter the score. No correction is made for comparing six candidates, so a qualifier is a candidate for a confirming run, not a proven improvement.

notes: Dev labels are reviewed (`labels_reviewed` is true; label source: scenarios).

Haiku failed the written calibration test (docs/DECISIONS.md entry 56, record JCAL-20261105T044839474906Z, 300 claims): agreement with Sonnet 0.813 against the local judge's 0.870, a paired difference of -0.057 (95% interval -0.110 to -0.006, wholly below zero), so it counts as clearly worse under the rule as written. It is still this record's judge by the coordinator's decision, because local judging was ruled out. The explanation (the local judge and Sonnet both say 'supported' to nearly everything, so the base rate helps the local agreement) is a reading, not proof. Sonnet is a reference, not ground truth. grounded_rate and unsupported_claim_rate come from Haiku through `claude -p`, one claim per call; no person has reviewed a sample, so they are not claims.
The injected-claim counts are a word-overlap proxy, not a reader's judgement.
3 candidates are compared with the baseline without a multiple-comparison correction.
